body:
THE CONTRACT IS `.adlc/specs/backlog-grooming.md`, committed on main (PR #993). Read it first — it carries the full pipeline, the verdict taxonomy, the autonomy model and all 21 acceptance criteria. The confirmed intent behind it is `docs/intent/backlog-grooming.md`. This ticket does not restate them; it records scope, rails and the build-order decisions a fresh agent needs.

WHAT IS BEING BUILT. Two artifacts:
1. `packages/backlog-groom/` — the portable core. `lib/` holds pure, injectable functions; `bin/backlog-groom.mjs` is the CLI. EVERY decision and EVERY rule is enforced here, never in the skill.
2. `.claude/skills/backlog-groom/SKILL.md` — the agentic wrapper that drives the CLI, supplies model judgment where the core asks for it, and runs the adversarial gate.

Repo-specific facts live in `.claude/backlog-groom-profile.json`, parsed by the core. JSON rather than markdown (deviating from `.claude/release-profile.md`) because it is machine-consumed and must fail closed on malformed input, which a prose file cannot do.

BUILD ORDER. The spec's §3 pipeline is the natural order and each stage is independently testable: fetch → classify → verify → cluster → rank → gate → floor → execute → report. Build and test each stage against the ACs that name it before starting the next. The gate (§3.6), the floor (§3.7) and execute (§3.8) are the risk concentration — they decide whether a live issue gets closed — so they get the most adversarial attention, not the most code.

PRECEDENTS TO FOLLOW, not reinvent. Read each before writing the equivalent:
- `packages/model-router/lib/floor.mjs` — the shape for §3.7's autonomy floor: ONE validator every entry point calls, disabling is explicit rather than accidental, invalid input is an operational error rather than a silent default. Note its comment on why `parseFloat` was rejected (it accepts `0.5abc`); the enum analogue is that an unknown action class must fail closed, never be dropped.
- `scripts/release-audit-collect.mjs` `fetchIssues` — the §3.1 fetch pattern AND the truncation-honesty rule: a response of exactly the fetch limit is reported as `truncated`, never accepted as complete.
- `scripts/ceremony-drift.mjs` — the §3.8 idempotency marker pattern; its module header explains why idempotence is the whole design constraint for a tool that writes to an issue.
- `scripts/release-audit-collect.mjs` `ticketsByIssueNumber` — an existing index from ADLC tickets to the GitHub issue they backlink to; reuse it rather than building a second one.

CONSUMERS. Nothing consumes this package yet — `issue-lanes` adoption is explicitly a separate ticket (spec §7). That makes the emitted set's schema the only external contract, which is why AC12 pins it against a committed fixture with a version field rather than against a live consumer.

THE TWO FAILURE MODES THAT MATTER MOST, both from the premortem and both already written into the spec — do not regress them while implementing:
- A mechanical check anchored to the cited LINE number closes live bugs (any unrelated edit above the citation shifts the lines below). The line is a hint; `fixed` requires the snippet to be absent from the WHOLE file (AC13).
- Enforcement that lives in the skill's prose is advisory, and an agent routes around advisory. The one-shot review property and the comment-before-act ordering are enforced in the core (AC14, AC17).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: all 26 in `.adlc/specs/backlog-grooming.md` §5, each with its own `verify:` command. They are the contract; this ticket adds none and removes none.

OUT OF SCOPE: filing new issues; modifying `issue-lanes` (its adoption of the emitted set is a follow-on ticket); reading issue comments as evidence (title and body only, mirroring the autopilot triage boundary); building a second ticket↔issue index.
title: Build @adlc/backlog-groom: code-grounded GitHub backlog grooming with a gated autonomy floor
